sessions.setting: Hallway of their apartment building on Valencia Street, running into each other on the way out

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Morning, Leo! I just got back from my run along the Embarcadero. Eight K, same as always. Churro was waiting at the door when I came back, howling like I'd abandoned him.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ha, sounds about right. Churro's got separation anxiety down to an art. When did you adopt him again, last October?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Yeah, from that rescue shelter in Daly City. Best decision ever, even if he does chew my running shoes. Are you heading out with Pixel?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Yep, evening walk at Dolores Park got pushed to morning today. Pixel's been restless since I got home late from the office last night.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: I love that we ended up in the same building. Makes it easy to coordinate when there's a late-night production issue.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Honestly, being neighbors on Valencia Street is one of the best perks of this whole startup thing. I can just knock on your door instead of Slacking you.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: True. Although last time you knocked at 11 PM about a deployment bug, I was already in my pajamas.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: And you still helped me debug it in fifteen minutes. That's why we make a good team.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Alright, I need to shower and get to the office. See you there?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Yeah, right after Pixel gets his park time. See you in an hour.

sessions.setting: Equinox gym on Market Street, during their morning workout

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You're three minutes late. I already started warming up on the rowing machine.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Sorry, I was dialing in my latest coffee roast before heading out. The Behmor 2000AB Plus is temperamental with Ethiopian beans — you have to watch the first crack like a hawk.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You and your home roasting. I swear you spend more time on coffee than some people spend cooking dinner.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Says the guy who spent six hours smoking a brisket last weekend. How's the beer coming, by the way?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: The Grainfather's been running nonstop in my garage. I'm doing a new West Coast IPA batch this weekend. Tweaking the hop schedule from my last brew.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Your garage in Temescal is basically a brewery at this point. Let me spot you on bench?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Yeah, let's do it. I need to be out by 8:15 — I'm picking up Maya for our carpool. Did you drive here?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: No, I Ubered. My Subaru's in the shop. Something with the brakes.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: My Rivian's out front if you need a ride after. That truck's been rock solid since I got it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The green R1T? I'll take you up on that. Alright, load up the bar, let's go.

sessions.setting: Yoga Tree on Hayes Street, chatting after their weekend class

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That pigeon pose at the end almost killed me today. I think my hips are tighter than usual from all the cycling.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: You're telling me — I walked here from my place in the Inner Sunset through Golden Gate Park, and my calves were already sore before class started.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Wait, you walk through the park to get to work too, right? That's such a nice commute.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Yeah, it's my favorite part of living in the Inner Sunset. Twenty-five minutes of trees and quiet before the chaos of the office. Hey, are you doing anything after this?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I've got ceramics tonight at the Clayroom on Valencia. It's my Wednesday ritual — I'm working on a new set of ramen bowls.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: That's so cool. I have my own Wednesday ritual — well, more like a weekend one. I bake sourdough every weekend. My starter is three years old now. I named her Naan.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You named your sourdough starter Naan? That's adorable.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: She's like a pet at this point. I feed her more reliably than some people feed their cats.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Don't let my cat Fika hear that — she'd be deeply offended. Should we grab a smoothie before we head out?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Definitely. There's a good place two blocks from here.

sessions.setting: Nadia's office at Caspian Labs in SoMa, one-on-one meeting

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Priya, hard to believe it's been almost four months since you started. I still remember meeting you at that Women in AI conference in Seattle last November.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: That feels like yesterday. You came up to me after my panel and basically pitched me on Caspian Labs on the spot.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Well, you'd just published that few-shot learning paper at ACL, and your talk about dialogue systems was exactly what we needed. I wasn't going to let MIT's finest slip away.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I'm glad you didn't. Finishing my master's at MIT last year and then jumping straight into a startup — it was a leap, but it's been worth it.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: You've been crushing it on the recommendation engine. Honestly, the quality of your work reminds me of why I left McKinsey to do this in the first place.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: The NLP specialization really prepared me for this kind of problem. How did you get the confidence to start Caspian Labs? Going from consulting to founding a company is a big jump.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Honestly? The Y Combinator Demo Day in March 2022 was the point of no return. We pitched, Sequoia gave us the Series A, and suddenly it was real. No going back after that.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Sequoia. That's incredible. I want to make sure I'm contributing at that level — what do you want me focused on this quarter?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: The citation extraction model. If we nail that, it becomes the cornerstone of the next product release.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I'm on it. I've already got some ideas on the architecture.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs office kitchen, end-of-day chat

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Nadia, I just finished the content calendar for Q2. We've come a long way since I joined a year ago in March.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: You really have. When I think back to co-founding Caspian Labs in January 2022 with that initial $2.1 million in seed funding, I never imagined we'd have a marketing operation this good.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Well, four years at Wired taught me how to tell a story. Tech journalism is basically marketing with more fact-checking.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: That's exactly why I wanted someone with your background. Speaking of stories — I need your help framing something. The Salesforce partnership talks are heating up.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: The AI assistant integration? How far along are the negotiations?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: We're in active negotiation. Their VP of product is pushing for an exclusive window, which I'm pushing back on. But if this goes through, it changes everything for us.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I'll start drafting the press materials now so we're ready to move fast. Anything else on your plate?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: I've got my Techstars mentoring session tomorrow. I mentor two women founders every quarter, and one of them just hit a rough fundraising patch. Reminds me of our early days.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You stretch yourself thin sometimes. CEO, mentor, marathon runner...

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: It keeps me sane, honestly. Alright, go home. Tell Walter I said hi.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Will do. He's probably chewed through another tennis ball by now.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs engineering area, their Tuesday pair-programming session

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Alright, Tuesday afternoon pair-programming time. Pull up the recommendation engine repo — I want to look at the embedding layer.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Already open. I've been thinking about how we can apply a similar approach to the citation extraction model I'm building. I just hit 91% F1 on our internal benchmarks, by the way.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ninety-one percent? That's phenomenal. How does it handle edge cases with ambiguous references?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Still some room to improve there. But the base architecture is solid. What language is the backend service running again?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Go. I use Go for all of Caspian's backend services. It's been my favorite language since I fell in love with goroutines at Berkeley.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Right, everything's in Go. That inference pipeline optimization you did in February was impressive — going from 340 milliseconds down to 87. How did you pull that off?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Mostly connection pooling and batching on the AWS side. The old pipeline was making individual inference calls. I just grouped them intelligently.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Smart. For the recommendation engine, I think we should try a similar batching approach for the vector lookups.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Agreed. Let's prototype it today. You handle the Python model layer, I'll write the Go service wrapper.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Perfect division of labor. Let's do it.

sessions.setting: Marcus's Rivian truck during their morning carpool to the SoMa office

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Morning! Walter, get in the back seat. Sorry, Maya, he's extra excited today.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I don't mind at all. Walter's the best part of our carpool. Does he really go to the office with you every single day?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Every day. The golden retriever is basically our unofficial mascot at this point. Nadia says he improves team morale by 200%.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: He does. I almost got a dog, but my studio on Folsom Street is too small. Fika takes up enough space as it is.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Your cat's a pretty good roommate though, from what you tell me. Did you go to the farmers market this morning?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Of course. Every Saturday on my Bianchi — Ferry Building Farmers Market is my ritual. I picked up some amazing persimmons. But today's Friday, so that was last week's haul I'm still working through.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: We should get some of those for the office kitchen. Traffic's looking light today — we'll be in SoMa in twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Good. I've got a packed morning. The new onboarding flow mockups are due to Nadia by noon.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: She'll love them. Your design work is always on point.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. Now tell Walter to stop licking my hand — I need it for Figma.

sessions.setting: Pandora Karaoke on Post Street, biweekly team karaoke night

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Finally, karaoke Friday! I've been looking forward to this all week. Who's picking the first song?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I'll go. But first — Nadia, how was the Napa Valley Marathon last weekend?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Three hours forty-two minutes! A personal best. My legs are still recovering but I'm riding the high.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Nice! I did the Big Sur Marathon the same weekend. Four hours eleven minutes. Not as fast as you, but the views made up for it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: You two are insane. I'll stick to volleyball, thanks. Hey Nadia, did you drive here?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Yeah, the Tesla's parked around the corner. The Model Y barely fits in these downtown spots.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Tell me about it. My Outback is wider than it looks. I had to park three blocks away.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: We do this every other Friday and you'd think we'd learn to take one car by now. Anyway, I'm singing 'Livin' on a Prayer' first and nobody can stop me.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Classic Nadia. I'm queuing up Stevie Wonder right after you.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I'll do my usual — 'Don't Stop Believin'.' It's Pandora Karaoke tradition at this point.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Alright, let's go. The room's booked for two hours. Marcus, order some edamame.

sessions.setting: Sightglass Coffee on 7th Street, working remotely together

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I love working from Sightglass. This is my favorite coffee shop for remote work — the light in here is perfect for design.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: The vibes are great. I'm trying to squeeze in some reading between pull requests. I'm almost at 250 entries in my book tracking database on Notion.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two hundred and fifty books? That's incredible. What are you reading right now?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Re-reading 'Godel, Escher, Bach' by Hofstadter. It's my all-time favorite. Every time I read it I find something new.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I've heard of it but never picked it up. I'm more of a visual person — I go through Moleskine sketchbooks instead of novels. I fill one every two months.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Physical sketchbooks! That's so analog for a digital designer.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I know, but there's something about pen on paper. It's like ceramics for me — the physical medium matters. Actually, a lot of my Figma templates started as sketches.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Wait, you publish Figma templates? I didn't know that.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Yeah, I've got twelve community templates up. Some of them get thousands of downloads. It's a nice creative outlet outside of work.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: That's two books a week for me, two sketchbooks a month for you. We're both compulsive documenters.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Kindred spirits. Want another oat latte? I'm going up.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Yes please. Extra shot.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs conference room, design review meeting

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Maya, the design sprint workshop you ran last week was phenomenal. Fourteen new feature concepts — that's a record for us.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Thanks, Nadia. I adapted the format from a workshop method I learned during my industrial design program at Konstfack in Stockholm.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: It shows. Your background in industrial design brings such a different perspective to software UX. It's not something I learned in my MBA at Stanford, that's for sure.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: And your business sense is something I definitely didn't get at Konstfack. Were you always interested in startups?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Not initially. I spent three years at McKinsey as a management consultant before I caught the bug. It was Leo who convinced me we should build something instead of advising others.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Well, I'm glad you did. Speaking of building — remember when I redesigned the dashboard back in January?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: How could I forget? User engagement jumped 35%. That was the inflection point for our retention metrics.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I want to apply the same principles to the new onboarding flow. The design sprint gave us three strong concepts for it.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Walk me through your top pick. I've got thirty minutes before my next call.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Sure. Let me pull up the wireframes.

sessions.setting: Mensho Tokyo ramen on Geary Boulevard, lunch break

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Man, Mensho Tokyo never disappoints. This is my favorite ramen spot in the city — the tori paitan is unreal.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You dragged me all the way to Geary for ramen, but I'll admit, this is worth it. How did you find this place?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A friend from my Berkeley CS days told me about it right after I graduated in 2017. Been coming ever since.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Berkeley to Caspian Labs — not a bad pipeline. I went to Howard for journalism. Different coasts, different worlds.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Where was Howard again?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: D.C. I grew up in Oakland though, so coming back to the Bay was always the plan. What'd you do this weekend?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I finished my custom mechanical keyboard build. Cherry MX Brown switches in a walnut case. The sound profile is chef's kiss.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You built a keyboard from scratch. Of course you did. Meanwhile, I've been trying to write. I'm working on a nonfiction book about the Oakland tech scene.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Really? How far along are you?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: About 40,000 words. It's slow going when you're also running marketing for a startup, but I chip away at it on weekends.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That's impressive. Let me know if you need any engineer perspectives for the book.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I might take you up on that. You ready to head back? We've got the product sync at 2.

sessions.setting: Walking through SoMa after leaving the office early on a Friday

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I keep meaning to tell you — I won the Kaggle Days championship back in February. I finally got the trophy in the mail.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Priya! That's amazing. You should have told me sooner. Competitions like that are huge. I made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list back in 2020 for enterprise tech, and that kind of recognition opens so many doors.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Forbes 30 Under 30, wow. You must have been, what, 28?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Yeah, I was still finding my footing in SF back then. I'd only moved here from Mexico City in August 2018. Everything felt new.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I can relate. Moving from Boston to San Francisco last year was a big adjustment for me. I grew up there — my parents still run their Indian grocery store in Cambridge. Sharma's Spice Market.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: I love that. Family businesses have such character. Do you miss the East Coast?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Sometimes. I miss my family, but I don't miss the winters. Plus, here I can speak to my parents in Hindi or Tamil whenever I need a taste of home.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: That's beautiful. I call my mom in Mexico City at least twice a week. Speaking three languages — English, Spanish, and some Portuguese — helps me stay connected too.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: You speak Portuguese too?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Conversational. Picked it up from Brazilian friends at Stanford. Want to grab dinner somewhere?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Sure, lead the way.

sessions.setting: Dolores Park, Leo walking Pixel while Maya is cycling past

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Leo! Hey! I was just finishing a training ride and spotted you from across the park.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Maya! Small world. I'm out here with Pixel — our evening walk. What are you training for?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The San Francisco Century Ride in September. A hundred miles. I've been building up endurance since I moved here from Stockholm in 2021, but this is the biggest challenge yet.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A hundred miles on a bike? That's hardcore. I can barely handle volleyball on Thursdays at Mission Playground.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Oh right, you play recreational volleyball! How's the team doing?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We're decent. Lost last week but it was close. Can you believe it's almost been a year since you joined Caspian? You started in June 2023, right?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Almost a year exactly, yeah. Joining as UX designer was the best decision I made after moving to the States. Hey, speaking of time — what are you up to on weekends these days?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I've been spending them on this open-source project — MilvusLite, a vector database. It's eating all my free time. I contribute every weekend.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A vector database? That sounds very you. Is it related to work?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Tangentially. It could improve our search infrastructure down the line. But for now it's just a passion project.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I get it. My ceramics are my version of that. Alright, I need to cool down before my legs cramp. See you at the office!

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: See you tomorrow!

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs office kitchen, morning coffee

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Morning, Priya. You're in early for a Friday.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I've got my Python teaching session at the SF Public Library tomorrow morning, and I want to prep some new exercises tonight. I volunteer as a TA there every Saturday.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: That's awesome. I do something similar — I mentor two high school students through Year Up in Oakland. It's the most rewarding thing I do outside of work.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: It really is. Teaching forces you to understand things at a deeper level. What are your students working on?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: One's interested in marketing, the other wants to do data science. I told the data science kid about you, actually. She was impressed.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Send her my way if she wants to chat. Hey, have you seen the blog numbers lately?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: We're on track. I launched the blog last year and we've been growing steadily. If the trend holds, we'll hit 50,000 monthly readers by August.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: That's incredible growth. I've been doing a side project too — training a personal GPT model on my own journal entries. It's fascinating how it captures writing patterns.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: A GPT on your journals? That's either brilliant or terrifying. Probably both. What gave you the idea?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Honestly? A podcast episode. Not your favorite one — what is it, 'How I Built This'?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Ha, you know me too well. Guy Raz is the best interviewer in the game.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I'll give it a listen sometime. Alright, back to the grind.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs co-founders' weekly sync in Nadia's office

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Okay, co-founder sync. Where are we on the Q3 engineering roadmap?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ahead of schedule, actually. The team's been firing on all cylinders. Hard to believe we've been at this since we founded Caspian Labs in 2022.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Two and a half years. Sometimes I look at you and still see the guy who pitched me on leaving consulting to build an AI company.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: And sometimes I still see the McKinsey consultant with the color-coded spreadsheets. We've come a long way. Speaking of the team — I think we need another senior engineer. Someone with production ML experience.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Your TensorFlow experience at Google was rare to find. Two years on that team gave you something you can't teach. We need someone similar.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I've been putting out feelers. Actually, remember the PennApps hackathon back in 2016? I got second place with that real-time speech translation app. My partner on that project just left Meta — she might be interested.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Reach out to her. We need people who can build under pressure. I was reading 'The Hard Thing About Hard Things' again last night — Horowitz talks about exactly this kind of hiring moment.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Still your favorite book?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Always. Every chapter feels more relevant as we grow. Okay, what about the infrastructure costs?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Down 30% since the AWS optimization. I'll have the full numbers by Monday.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Good. Send them over. I'll fold them into the board deck.

sessions.setting: Golden Gate Park, Caspian Labs July 4th barbecue

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Alright, the brisket's been smoking since 5 AM. My signature smoked brisket — twelve hours, low and slow. Who's ready?

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: It smells incredible, Marcus. I brought my mole poblano — cooked it last night. It's my grandmother's recipe. I make it every Sunday, but I figured today deserved a special batch.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Nadia, you cook mole every Sunday? That's dedication. I can barely manage pasta on weeknights.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: It's my way of staying connected to Mexico City. My brother Marco thinks mine is better than abuela's, but don't tell her that.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You have a brother? I don't think you've mentioned him.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Yeah, Marco. He's younger than me — works as an architect in Guadalajara. We talk every week.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That's sweet. My brother Erik is in Sweden too — marine biologist at Uppsala. We FaceTime but it's hard with the time zones.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: My mom would love this gathering. She's a retired principal from Oakland Unified — she always says the best community building happens around food.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: She sounds wonderful. Oh, speaking of family — it's Fika's first birthday this month! I adopted her from the SF SPCA last March and she's turned into the neediest cat alive.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: We should get her a little party hat. Marcus, cut the brisket — I'm starving.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Coming right up. Plates are on the table.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs break room, after their Tuesday pair-programming session

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Good session today. Hey, before you head out — did you read that new paper from DeepMind on context windows?

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Not yet. Is it on your morning reading list?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Yeah, I read a research paper every morning before work and annotate it in Notion. It's the only way I keep up with the field.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I should adopt that habit. Right now I just binge papers on weekends. How was your trip to Kyoto, by the way? You went in March, right?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: It was wonderful. Two weeks with my grandparents. My obaachan made me promise to visit more often. She's 87 and still tends her garden every morning.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: That's beautiful. My brother Ravi keeps trying to get me to visit Boston more too. He's a cardiologist at Mass General — works crazy hours but always makes time when I'm there.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A cardiologist! That's intense. My sister Yumi has a demanding job too — she's a product manager at Apple in Cupertino. We try to meet up once a month for dinner.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Small world — Apple and a startup in the same family. Hey, is it still nice out? I rode my bike today.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The red Specialized? Yeah, it's clear. Perfect riding weather.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: The Allez, yeah. It's my commute bike when the weather cooperates. Alright, I'm heading out. See you at standup tomorrow.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: See you. Tell Bayes I said... wait, you don't have Bayes yet. Never mind. See you tomorrow.

sessions.setting: Renegade Craft Fair preview event at Fort Mason, Maya showing Marcus around

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Marcus, thanks for coming to the preview. The actual fair is next weekend, but I wanted to show you my booth setup.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Of course. I still can't believe you went from industrial design in Stockholm to selling ceramics at craft fairs. You graduated from Konstfack, right?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Yeah, 2019. My dad's a furniture maker in Gothenburg — he's the one who taught me to work with my hands. Ceramics was a natural extension of that.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Well, your bowls are beautiful. How much are you selling them for?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Eighty-five dollars each. I've got three that I think will sell at the fair. They're glazed with this ash technique I've been perfecting.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: You should let me feature you on the Caspian blog. 'Startup designer moonlights as ceramic artist' — it's a great story. Speaking of awards, didn't you win something for design?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A Red Dot Design Award in 2020, for a modular standing desk concept. That feels like a lifetime ago.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: See? I knew it. We creative types need our outlets. Mine's home brewing — my IPA 'Foghorn' won a silver medal at the Oakland Homebrew Festival last year.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Foghorn! That's a perfect name. You should bring some to the fair.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I'll bring a growler. My sister Denise is visiting from D.C. that weekend too — she's a civil rights attorney there. She'd love this scene.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Bring her along! The more the merrier. Okay, help me move this display table two inches to the left.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: On it.

sessions.setting: Caspian Labs main conference room, technical planning meeting

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Okay, let's talk about the international expansion. We're starting to get inbound interest from Latin America, and I can handle the Spanish communications myself. I also speak conversational Portuguese, so Brazil is doable too.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That's a huge advantage. My parents would love to hear about this — they run Tanaka Gardens, the bonsai nursery back in San Jose. They've always said the best businesses are the ones that can cross borders.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I can help with Hindi and Tamil-speaking markets if we ever expand to India. I speak both fluently.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: That's good to know, Priya. Since you joined in December, you've consistently surprised me with how much you bring beyond pure data science.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Speaking of which — remember those chai masala cookies I brought to the holiday party? They sold out in fifteen minutes. I'm thinking we should do more team food events.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Those cookies were incredible. I ate four of them.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: My mom would approve. She's a pediatrician at Hospital Infantil de Mexico in Mexico City — she always says food is the best medicine for team bonding.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Your mom's a doctor? I had no idea. My parents are just humble bonsai growers from San Jose.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Every family has its own kind of wisdom. Alright, back to the expansion plan. Leo, what's the engineering lift for multi-language support?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Moderate. Give me two sprints and I can have the localization framework ready.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I'll start prepping the NLP models for multilingual input. We should prioritize Spanish and Portuguese first.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Agreed. Let's reconvene next week with a concrete timeline.

sessions.setting: Bespoke Events space in SoMa, after Caspian Labs' first user conference wraps up

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Three hundred attendees! I can't believe we actually pulled it off. Caspian Labs' first user conference is in the books.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: Marcus, you organized this entire thing. Take a bow.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: The turnout was insane. Oh, and on a personal note — I adopted a rabbit last month! His name is Bayes. He's from the House Rabbit Society.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You named your rabbit Bayes? Of course you did. My brother Erik — the marine biologist at Uppsala — would say that's peak scientist behavior.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: I'll take that as a compliment. Erik's at Uppsala University, right? Do you visit him much?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Once a year when I go back to Sweden. I miss it, but San Francisco's been good to me. I've even been learning Mandarin at a night school in the Richmond District — three languages now. Swedish, English, and basic Mandarin.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Impressive. I've got English and my intermediate French from a semester abroad in Lyon. But three languages is solid. Hey Leo, you're quiet — everything okay?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Just taking it all in. When I graduated from Berkeley CS in 2017, I never imagined I'd be co-running a company with 300 people at our conference.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: It is surreal. I'm going to celebrate tomorrow with pickup basketball at Lake Merritt. Anyone want in?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I'll stick with my volleyball, thanks.

turns.speaker: nadia
turns.text: And I'll stick with my morning run. But tonight — tonight we celebrate. Drinks are on Caspian Labs.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Best boss ever.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Agreed. To Caspian Labs!

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: To Caspian Labs!
